images.name: cover
images.title: How to hire an *AI Employee*
images.sub: Write the job, sort the duties, test it on real cases and supervise the first month, in that order.

images.name: steps
images.title: Hiring an AI Employee, *step by step*
steps: Every duty, how often it happens each month, and the systems it touches.
Does it alone, does it and reports back, or asks a person first.
Software you assemble yourself, or a provider that builds and maintains it.
30 to 50 cases from last month, including the awkward ones.
Give it only the logins it needs
Its own user in each system, with the narrowest permissions.
A person approves its work, then duties move to "alone" one at a time.
One person reads its log weekly and keeps its rules current.

images.name: authority
images.title: A front desk job, *sorted by authority*
rows: Sends them from the calendar and logs each one
Follows up by text and email on a schedule
Replies from the written policies, sends a daily summary
Moves the booking and fills the gap from the waitlist
Collects the details and hands them to the manager
Prepares the request for a person to approve

images.name: build-or-provider
images.title: Build it yourself *or use a provider*
head: Assemble it yourself
Provider builds it
rows: Usually a monthly fee, sometimes a setup fee
Simple rules, common systems, a technical person with time
Phone work, several systems or sensitive records
images.source: Compare either one with the full cost of the seat

images.name: first-month
images.title: The first month, *week by week*
rows: Draft mode: it prepares every reply and action, a person approves each one
Rules updated from every change the person made in week 1
Confirmations and reminders move to "does it alone"
Routine questions move to "reports back"; money and complaints stay with a person
One short log review a week, and rule updates when the business changes

images.name: quote
images.text: Most failed setups skip straight to the software. *Start with the job description.*
